name: Disodium cocoamphodiacetate
description: Disodium cocoamphodiacetate (CAS 68650-39-5 ), also known as DSCADA or DSCAD, is an amphoteric surfactant derived from coconut oil fatty acids. It functions as a foam booster, secondary surfactant, and conditioning agent across personal care and industrial cleaning formulations. In shampoos, body washes, and facial cleansers, it enhances foam texture and improves mildness when combined with primary anionic surfactants such as SLES. Liquid hand soaps and baby care products rely on it to reduce irritation potential. This surfactant helps maintain effective cleansing performance while protecting sensitive skin. In household and industrial cleaning concentrates, it supports emulsification of oils and greases, improving soil removal on hard surfaces. Formulators in adhesives and coatings also use it as a dispersing aid where compatibility across a broad pH range is a formulation requirement. Its versatility makes it a staple in modern chemical manufacturing and product development. Disodium cocoamphodiacetate is supplied as an aqueous solution, typically at 40–50% active content. It is available in technical and cosmetic grades, with cosmetic-grade material meeting purity standards relevant to personal care applications. Bulk supply is standard in drums and IBCs, with tank delivery available for high-volume industrial buyers.
